To explore the scaling potential of Agentic Deep Research, we aim to establish a scalable training framework as a mandatory first step. Current paradigms that rely on high-latency, unstable online interactions fundamentally bottleneck this process. In this section, we present our LiteResearcher framework, which decouples agent evolution from the open web while ensuring generalization to real-world web dynamics. As illustrated in Figure [2](#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4 Methods: Towards Scalable Training ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent"), the ecosystem is built upon three core pillars:

(1) Co-construct Training Data and Corpus Pipeline: To achieve diversity in the data distribution and scalability in data quantity, we propose a unified framework that co-evolves the training data and the local corpus.

(2) Stable Local Tool Environment: Leveraging the enriched webpage corpus, we construct a Local Search Engine and Local Browse Tool that mirror the behavior of real-world search dynamics within the synthesized data.

(3) Difficulty-Aware Curriculum Learning: To continuously expand the model’s capability boundaries, we leverage our unlimited synthetic data pool to implement a multi-stage curriculum that serves the model with data of appropriate difficulty, thereby ensuring sustainable performance improvements.

![Refer to caption](2604.17931v2/x2.png)

Figure 2: System architecture overview. (a) Corpus Extension and QA Synthesis: An iterative data engine which also enriches local webpage corpus, powering stable, local tools for zero-cost agent RL training. (b) Reinforcement Curriculum Learning: Synthetic tasks are leveled by complexity to guide the agent through progressive training stages. This reinforcement learning loop utilizes local tool interactions, scaling research capabilities while effectively preventing training saturation.

Table 1: Five atomic search capabilities fundamental to complex deep research.

### 4.1 Co-construct Training Data and Corpus Pipeline

We identify that complex real-world deep research trajectories are fundamentally composed of five atomic search capabilities:

* •

  Direct Information: Directly finding a specific piece of information via search.
* •

  Aggregation: Locating a target answer based on multiple identifying attributes.
* •

  Enumeration: Listing and counting all entities that satisfy specific constraints.
* •

  Cross-verification: Validating and triangulating claims across independent sources.
* •

  Statistics: Performing comprehensive calculations and extracting numerical metrics.

To construct a dataset with both capability diversity and scalability, rather than relying on complex, handcrafted generation logic, we first scale up the underlying information sources to comprehensively cover the diverse search patterns of the real world. Subsequently, we filter this vast information pool into solvable, high-quality tasks. Specifically:

#### QA generation from Seed Corpus

The data construction process begins with a high-quality Seed Corpus including Wikipedia and BBC News articles. We then prompt an LLM with the template in Appendix [A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Extract Information and Compose QA Prompt ‣ Appendix A Synthetic Data ‣ 6 Conclusions ‣ Contribution of RL over SFT. ‣ Effectiveness of Multi-Stage Training. ‣ On-Policy vs. Off-Policy Training. ‣ Local Environment vs. Live Internet. ‣ 5.3 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent")
to process this raw content and extract structured question-answer (QA) pairs that target key factual entities within the content. These initial QA pairs serve as the foundational “seed tasks” that trigger the subsequent iterative expansion of the local environment.

#### Information Source Masking

To prevent the agent from relying on trivial shortcuts, we implement a source masking mechanism. After a QA pair is generated, we deliberately delete its original information source from the local corpus. This forces the agent to navigate the expanded corpus to discover alternative, non-trivial search pathways, naturally eliciting the complex atomic search capabilities detailed in Table [1](#S4.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 4 Methods: Towards Scalable Training ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent").

#### Strict Quality and Difficulty Filtering

To guarantee the quality and solvability of the dataset, the candidate QA pairs undergo a rigorous LLM-based evaluation guided by a 7-point rubric (Appendix [A.2](#A1.SS2 "A.2 Rubric filter Prompt ‣ Appendix A Synthetic Data ‣ 6 Conclusions ‣ Contribution of RL over SFT. ‣ Effectiveness of Multi-Stage Training. ‣ On-Policy vs. Off-Policy Training. ‣ Local Environment vs. Live Internet. ‣ 5.3 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent")). As detailed in Appendix [A.2](#A1.SS2 "A.2 Rubric filter Prompt ‣ Appendix A Synthetic Data ‣ 6 Conclusions ‣ Contribution of RL over SFT. ‣ Effectiveness of Multi-Stage Training. ‣ On-Policy vs. Off-Policy Training. ‣ Local Environment vs. Live Internet. ‣ 5.3 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent"), this rubric contains dimensions such as independence, ambiguity, answer verifiability, etc. A data point is retained only if it strictly satisfies all seven criteria. Furthermore, prior to each training session, we apply an additional difficulty filter to ensure the tasks are appropriately calibrated to the agent’s current capability (see Section 4.3). This final distillation process provides a diverse and realistic data distribution for subsequent training.

#### Continuously Expanding Corpus

For each filtered QA pair, we utilize a search engine to fetch related webpages from the live internet. These newly retrieved pages are continuously appended to the Enriched Corpus. This iterative expansion creates a corpus covering the vast and diverse information distribution of the real world.

### 4.2 Stable Local Tool Environment

Leveraging the enriched corpus from Section [4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Co-construct Training Data and Corpus Pipeline ‣ 4 Methods: Towards Scalable Training ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent") ($\sim$32M pages, 1M+ domains), we build a fully local tool environment that replaces online interaction during RL training. Unlike standard RAG pipelines that split each page into many chunks, we adopt page-level indexing: each webpage is represented by a single vector (title + summary). This keeps the index small enough to serve hundreds of concurrent rollouts at low latency, which would be infeasible with a chunk-level index that is $\sim$10$\times$ larger. During training, the system sustains hundreds of concurrent tool requests, accumulating to 73.2M calls over the full RL run (Section [5](#S5 "5 Experiments ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent")). The corpus is served through two purpose-built services (infrastructure details in Appendix [D](#A4 "Appendix D Infrastructure Details ‣ 6 Conclusions ‣ Contribution of RL over SFT. ‣ Effectiveness of Multi-Stage Training. ‣ On-Policy vs. Off-Policy Training. ‣ Local Environment vs. Live Internet. ‣ 5.3 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent")):

* •

  Local Search Engine: We adopt BGE-M3 (Chen et al., [2024](#bib.bib3)) for hybrid retrieval, which produces both dense and learned sparse embeddings in a single forward pass. The two signals are fused at query time through the built-in hybrid search of Milvus (Wang et al., [2021](#bib.bib36)). All embeddings are stored on disk and accessed via DiskANN (Jayaram Subramanya et al., [2019](#bib.bib11)) with mmap, achieving $\sim$0.15 s/query ($\sim$10$\times$ faster than online search engine).
* •

  Local Browse Tool: Full webpage content is stored as Markdown in PostgreSQL, keyed by URL and tuned for 1,000 concurrent connections; pages are returned directly upon request at $\sim$0.17 s/page ($\sim$46$\times$ faster than Jina Reader).

### 4.3 Difficulty-Aware Curriculum Learning

A fundamental challenge in Agentic RL is training saturation, where the reward curve converges because the model becomes trapped at a difficulty threshold, correctly solving easy tasks while completely failing complex ones, resulting in no meaningful learning gradient.

#### Difficulty-Aware Data Filtering

To address training saturation, before each RL stage, we evaluate the difficulty of training queries. For each query, we generate $K=8$ rollouts (pass@8) and strictly retain only those where the number of correct responses $c$ satisfies $1\leq c\leq 7$. Queries with $c=8$ are discarded as trivial (yielding zero useful gradient), while those with $c=0$ are deemed impossible or excessively noisy.

#### On-Policy GRPO Curriculum Learning

We employ the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (Shao et al., [2024](#bib.bib28)) framework. Given a query $q$ and sampled outputs ${o_{1},\dots,o_{K}}$, the advantage $A_{i}$ is computed by normalizing the reward of $o_{i}$ against the group mean and standard deviation. Stripped of KL and entropy terms, our objective function is defined strictly as the clipped surrogate loss:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | $\mathcal{J}_{GRPO}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{q\sim P(Q),{o_{i}}_{i=1}^{K}\sim\pi_{\theta_{old}}}\left[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}\min\left(r_{i}(\theta)A_{i},\text{clip}\left(r_{i}(\theta),1-\epsilon_{low},1+\epsilon_{high}\right)A_{i}\right)\right]$ |  |

where $r_{i}(\theta)=\frac{\pi_{\theta}(o_{i}|q)}{\pi_{\theta_{rollout}}(o_{i}|q)}$ is the probability ratio of training engine and rollout engine. While standard implementations perform multiple mini-batch updates over a replay buffer, we enforce a strictly on-policy update. We present a detailed ablation study regarding this completely on-policy formulation in Section [5](#S5 "5 Experiments ‣ LiteResearcher: A Scalable Agentic RL Training Framework for Deep Research Agent").
